_note: Per-type EDITORIAL Vega-Lite recipe skeletons — what the Programmer fills in from analyst.json data_tables + designer.json. These are spec FRAGMENTS, not full specs: mark + key encoding notes + what to highlight + editorial defaults. They EXTEND component_implementations.json charts_vega_lite (don't restate width:container / centering / scale.zero / labelExpr mechanics — those live there). Always: inline data; "width":"container"; de-clutter via axis_label_polish.json config; annotate via annotation_layers.json; color via design_tokens.json data_color_scales + --accent for the highlighted datum.
_sources: Vega-Lite documentation + gallery (mark/encoding idioms, re-authored). FT Visual Vocabulary (which chart for which intent). Project component_implementations.json (mechanics this extends).
_cdn: MANDATORY — load Vega from the PINNED BUILD-FILE URL form, never the bare-package form. Bare-package jsDelivr URLs (e.g. https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/vega@5) are served WITHOUT a JS content-type, so Chrome blocks them with net::ERR_BLOCKED_BY_ORB and every chart renders blank. Use exactly these three, in order: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/vega@5.30.0/build/vega.min.js , https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/vega-lite@5.21.0/build/vega-lite.min.js , https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/vega-embed@6.26.0/build/vega-embed.min.js . The pinned `@x.y.z/build/<pkg>.min.js` shape is the only form proven to render clean — keep versions current-stable as pinned here; do NOT regress to `@5` / `@latest` / a `/+esm` import.

_global_defaults.width: "width": "container" (responsive) BUT embed it through the canonical responsive embedChart() helper (component_implementations.json -> charts_vega_lite.responsive_embed): bare width:container is measured during inline parse and returns 0 on heavy pages, rendering an invisible 0-width chart. Composite/faceted charts set explicit child width + spacing and are centered via .vega-embed svg{margin:0 auto} (component_implementations.json).
_global_defaults.config: Apply the de-clutter config block from axis_label_polish.json (view.stroke=null, axis grid/ticks/domain off as specified, legend.orient='top', legend.title=null).
_global_defaults.color: Default to muted/grey marks; color ONLY the highlighted datum with --accent (conditional encoding, annotation_layers.json highlight_key_datum). Sequential/diverging/categorical scales -> design_tokens.json data_color_scales (set scale.range or scale.scheme).
_global_defaults.tooltip: "tooltip": true (or an explicit tooltip array of the fields the reader needs) on the primary mark.
_global_defaults.highlight_note: Every recipe names a 'highlight' — wire it to content.highlight from designer.json.

encoding: Horizontal (long labels / many items): y = category (nominal, sort by value: "sort": "-x"), x = value (quantitative).
Vertical column: x = category (sort "-y"), y = value.
ALWAYS sort by value not alphabetically (encoding_craft.json sort_by_value).
bar.highlight: Conditional fill: the story's item = --accent, all others = --muted/grey (annotation_layers.json). Optionally a text mark with the value at the bar end.
editorial_defaults: Bars start at ZERO — no scale.zero=false here (axis_label_polish.json zero_baseline_rule).
Drop the axis with the category labels' gridlines/ticks; keep light gridlines only on the value axis.
Value labels at bar ends can replace the value-axis entirely for a handful of bars.

encoding: x = primary category (nominal), xOffset = sub-group (nominal)  [xOffset gives native grouped bars], y = value.
Or facet by the secondary dimension for many groups (see small_multiples_facet).
color = sub-group via a categorical scale (design_tokens.json categorical).
grouped_bar.highlight: Accent the one sub-group/category the narrative compares; grey the rest. Keep the legend on top, no title.
editorial_defaults: Use xOffset (Vega-Lite native grouping), not manual x math.
Cap at ~2-4 sub-groups before grouped bars get noisy — beyond that, small multiples.
Consistent sub-group color + order across every group.

stacked_bar.intent: part_to_whole | composition over a few categories/time
encoding: x (or y) = category/time, y (or x) = value with "stack": true, color = segment (categorical).
For 100%-stacked share: "stack": "normalize" (proportional_stacked_bar).
stacked_bar.highlight: Accent the segment that carries the story; consider a text mark labeling that segment's share. Order segments by a fixed semantic order, largest-first if none.
editorial_defaults: normalize when the message is SHARE; absolute stack when the message is TOTAL+composition.
Keep stack order identical across categories so segments are comparable.
100%-stacked hides absolutes — surface the total in a callout if it matters (chart_chooser.json).

mark.point: false (add point:true only for sparse series or to mark observations)

encoding: x = time (temporal; set axis format via labelExpr/format — Vega-expr not JS), y = value (quantitative), color = series (categorical) IF few series.
Lines MAY truncate: "scale": {"zero": false} + an explicit domain on y (axis_label_polish.json) — a line shows change, not magnitude-from-zero.
line.highlight: Label the line END with a text+argmax mark instead of a legend for few series (annotation_layers.json line_end_label). Mark the key turning point with a rule + text.
editorial_defaults: > ~4-5 lines = spaghetti -> highlight one in --accent + grey the rest (a detail/overview layer), or switch to small multiples.
scale.zero=false is allowed and usually right for lines.
Light major Y gridlines only; no X gridlines.

encoding: x = time, y = value ("stack": true for composition), color = series.
Single-series area: fill with a muted --accent tint; the edge in --accent.
For deviation-over-time: two areas split at a baseline by sign (chart_chooser.json surplus_deficit_line).
area.highlight: Accent the focal band; for stacked area watch occlusion — if lower bands vanish, switch to lines or small multiples.
editorial_defaults: Stacked AREA only with few, smoothly-varying series; otherwise stacked columns.
Area implies magnitude -> y SHOULD include zero for a single filled series (unlike a plain line).

layered_line.intent: change_over_time with a reference / forecast band / event
encoding: Layer order: bands/reference rules at the BOTTOM, data line in the MIDDLE, annotations (text/point) on TOP.
Forecast: a fan of nested confidence areas (low opacity) under the central line (chart_chooser.json fan_chart).
Reference/threshold lines + event markers from annotation_layers.json (rule mark).
layered_line.highlight: The data line in --accent over muted reference geometry; label the end + the key event.
editorial_defaults: Resolve scales explicitly when layers share an axis.
Keep reference geometry visually quiet so the data reads first.

slope.mark: layer: line (two x positions per item) + point at each end + text label at ends
encoding: x = the two time points / conditions (ordinal, just two values), y = value, detail/color = item.
x axis: only two ticks; drop everything else.
slope.highlight: Accent the 1-2 items that rose/fell most; grey the rest. Label item names at the right end (or both ends).
editorial_defaults: No gridlines; two x labels only; direct labels, no legend.
If many lines cross into a hairball, highlight a few and grey the field.

encoding: Ranking: y = category (sort by value), x = value — one dot per item (a de-inked bar).
Distribution: x = value, y = group (or a constant), one dot per observation; add small jitter/yOffset to reduce overplot.
dot_strip.highlight: Accent the focal dot(s); optionally a connecting rule from a baseline (-> lollipop).
editorial_defaults: Prefer dot strip over bars when there are MANY items (less ink).
For pairs (before/after per category) connect the two dots with a rule (a 'dumbbell').

lollipop.mark: layer: rule (stem from baseline to value) + point (the head)
encoding: Horizontal: y = category (sort by value), rule x = 0 -> x2 = value, point x = value.
The head carries the eye; the stem carries the magnitude (length channel).
lollipop.highlight: Accent the focal item's stem+head; grey the rest. Value label beside the head if few items.
editorial_defaults: Stem starts at ZERO (it encodes magnitude by length).
Use when bars feel heavy but you still want length, not just position.

small_multiples_facet.intent: compare the SAME chart across many groups (any intent) — the spaghetti antidote
small_multiples_facet.mark: any (line/bar/area); set on the inner spec
encoding: "facet": {"field": group, "type": "nominal", "columns": N} at the TOP level (columns belongs on the facet spec top level, NOT inside the facet object — component_implementations.json).
Inner spec: explicit width/height per panel + shared encodings; "resolve": {"scale": {"y": "shared"}} so panels are comparable.
Sort facets by a meaningful order (peak value, total), not alphabetical.
small_multiples_facet.highlight: In every panel, grey all series and accent the focal one; or accent the panel that is the story. A shared scale makes the comparison honest.
editorial_defaults: Faceted charts ignore width:container and render at panel width -> center the SVG (component_implementations.json).
Keep axes minimal in inner panels; one shared axis where possible.
Shared y-scale unless the per-panel SHAPE (not level) is the point.

encoding: x = category/time-bin (nominal/ordinal), y = category (nominal), color = value (quantitative, sequential scale).
Calendar: x = week-of-year, y = day-of-week, color = daily value.
color scale = sequential from design_tokens.json (NOT a rainbow); set a clear legend with units.
heatmap.highlight: Outline the focal cell(s) with a rule/stroke; optionally text marks of the value in the most extreme cells.
editorial_defaults: Sequential (one direction) or diverging (around a midpoint) color only — never categorical hues for ordered magnitude (encoding_craft.json).
Square-ish cells; readable gaps; values as text only where they aid reading.
Sort rows/cols by a summary (cluster-like) order, not alphabetical, when it reveals structure.

strip_beeswarm.intent: distribution — show EVERY observation without overplotting
encoding: x = value (quantitative), y = group (nominal) or constant; add yOffset jitter to spread points.
True beeswarm packing (no overlap, no random jitter) is not a native transform — approximate with jitter/offset; if exact packing is required, that is a D3 force task (d3_fallback_recipes.json note).
Overlay a rule/tick at the median or mean if a summary helps.
strip_beeswarm.highlight: Accent the focal observation(s); keep the cloud muted and semi-transparent.
editorial_defaults: Transparency + jitter beats a solid blob.
Show every point when n is small/medium; switch to histogram/density only when n is large.

connected_scatter.intent: correlation over time | change_over_time as a path
connected_scatter.mark: layer: line (ordered by time) + point (each year) + text (label start/end/key years)
encoding: x = variable A, y = variable B, "order": time (so the line connects in time order), detail = series.
Both axes usually scale.zero=false (relationship, not magnitude).
connected_scatter.highlight: Label the first, last, and turning-point years; accent the path; arrowhead at the latest point to show direction.
editorial_defaults: Direction matters -> mark start and end clearly.
Keep to one trajectory (or a few highlighted); many become unreadable.

encoding: x, y = two quantitative variables; both usually scale.zero=false.
Bubble: size = third quantitative variable — Vega-Lite size is AREA by default (correct); do NOT pre-square or map to radius (encoding_craft.json area_not_radius).
color = category (hue) if a 4th, ordered dimension -> use shade not hue.
Optional trend layer (regression transform) UNDER the points.
scatter_bubble.highlight: Accent + label the focal point(s); mute the field. Tooltip carries the exact x/y (and size) values.
editorial_defaults: scale.zero=false on both axes is normal for relationships (axis_label_polish.json).
Set a size legend with real value anchors so readers can decode area.
Many overlapping points -> add opacity or switch to a 2D histogram/heatmap.

choropleth.intent: spatial — a NORMALIZED value by region
choropleth.mark: geoshape (Vega-Lite geoshape over inlined TopoJSON/GeoJSON) OR Leaflet GeoJSON (component_implementations.json maps_leaflet) for interactive pan/zoom
encoding: shape = the region geometry (inline geo), color = a NORMALIZED metric (rate / per-capita / density), sequential or diverging scale.
A choropleth must NOT encode raw counts (big regions dominate) — for counts use a proportional-symbol map (chart_chooser.json spatial).
choropleth.highlight: Outline / accent the focal region(s); a clear legend with units and a sensible bin/threshold scheme.
editorial_defaults: Reuse ONE sequential scale (design_tokens.json) consistent with any bars/callouts of the same metric.
Decide continuous vs binned (quantize) — binned reads more honestly for skewed data.
If interaction (zoom, hover popups) is wanted, build with Leaflet, not geoshape.
